We need to propose a retrosynthesis route for target SMILES: O=S(NC1=CC(N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2)=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1)(C5=C(F)C=CC=C5)=O

We must use templates in order: ['20810', '2895', '1914397', '1914398', '1914399', '74054'] and at least 6 reactions. So each template corresponds to a step. We need to construct a tree JSON where root is target molecule, then reaction using template 20810 gives two precursors (as we saw from apply_template). Then each precursor further broken down using next template, etc. Must have at least 6 reactions, we have exactly 6 templates, so each step is one reaction.

We need to apply sequentially: step1: target -> apply template 20810 gives precursors: from earlier result: ('CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1', 'O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1F') Wait result: "(('CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1', 'O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1F'),)". So two fragments: fragment A (complex amine) and fragment B (sulfonyl chloride with fluorophenyl). Good.

Step2: apply template 2895 to fragment A? Actually template 2895 is a nitro to amine? Let's see its retro smarts: It converts a phenyl with -NH2 to nitro? Actually retro smarts: [C:7]-[#8:6]-[c:5]1...>>O=[N+;H0;D3:1](-[O-])-[c:2]1... So forward reaction is nitro to phenoxy? Wait retro means we go from product to precursors. So applying to fragment A (which contains an aniline N) will give nitro precursor? The apply_template we did on fragment A gave product with nitro group: 'CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1' So step2: fragment A -> nitro aromatic precursor plus same rest.

Thus after step2 we have two precursors: the same amide side chain (unchanged) and nitro aromatic? Actually apply_template returned a single product (the transformed molecule) as precursor? It gave a tuple with one SMILES: the nitro version. So reaction 2 takes fragment A and produces nitro aromatic precursor (call fragment A2). So we need to keep the other fragment (maybe unchanged). In retrosynthesis tree, each reaction node's children are precursors. For step1 we had two children. For step2 we need to replace the fragment A node with a reaction node using template 2895, whose children are the nitro precursor (fragment A2) and maybe other fragments? The template likely splits off something? But result shows only one product, meaning the reaction is a transformation of the aromatic amine to nitro, no extra fragments. So children: one molecule (nitro). So the tree will have depth.

Step3: apply template 1914397 to fragment A2 (nitro aromatic). We applied and got two fragments: ('CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCNCC1', 'O=[N+]([O-])c1cc(Br)c2c(c1)CCC1(CCC1)O2'). So step3 splits into amide side chain (simplified) and brominated aromatic with nitro.

Step4: apply template 1914398 to the brominated nitro aromatic (the second fragment). We applied and got ('BrBr', 'O=[N+]([O-])c1ccc2c(c1)CCC1(CCC1)O2'). So splits into BrBr (bromine?) and the same aromatic without Br? Actually product: BrBr (bromine molecule) and the aromatic without Br (still nitro). So step4 yields two precursors: BrBr (maybe Br2) and the aromatic nitro.

Step5: apply template 1914399 to the aromatic nitro (without Br). We applied and got ('O=C1CC2(CCC2)Oc2ccc([N+](=O)[O-])cc21',). That's a single precursor (a lactone fused aromatic nitro). So step5 transforms to that.

Step6: apply template 74054 to that precursor to break into three fragments: from template mapping, it splits a carbonyl attached to aromatic etc into three pieces: O=[C]... etc. Let's apply to see result.
